picks.intervention_label: trastuzumab deruxtecan (T-DXd), continue pending HER2 reconciliation
picks.rationale: Three validated IHC 3+ results are the strongest predictive biomarker this tumor has ever produced, and in the central IHC 3+ population T-DXd hit ORR 61.3% (95% CI 49.4-72.4) with mDOR 22.1 months. Two zero Signatera draws right after SBRT and the first doses are at least consistent with the drug working. I would not walk away from that on the strength of a weak signal from a research-grade MXIF panel that is not a validated HER2 assay. Continue with maximal antiemetic prophylaxis and tight ILD surveillance until the 2026-08 re-stain tier and the next ctDNA draws give an actual reason to stop.
primary_concerns: Adjudicated drug-related ILD was 10.5% with three deaths in DESTINY-PanTumor02, and the unresolved 2026-03 outside CT read for fibrosis would put him in the pre-existing-lung-comorbidity risk group if it is right; the CT discrepancy has to be resolved, not waved off.
Severe nausea after dose 2 is an active dose-limiting problem; dose reduction is the modal fix in the pooled trials (22.6% reduced at 5.4 mg/kg) but it may not be enough here.
If the pending re-stain comes back HER2-low, the on-label 3+ case collapses to breast-cancer extrapolation and my ranking with it.
The bladder IHC 3+ subgroup is 16 patients, so the tier-matched estimate is wide.

picks.intervention_label: LY4052031 (Nectin-4 ADC, topoisomerase I payload) — NEXUS-01 cohort B2, NCT06465069
picks.rationale: Nectin-4 gave this patient his 25-month complete response, and the resistance biology says post-EV progression usually leaves the antigen standing: retained expression in post-EV biopsies, efflux and uptake defects rather than antigen loss. Cohort B2 requires prior enfortumab vedotin instead of excluding it, the camptothecin payload avoids MMAE and its neuropathy, and the initial post-EV response rate was 47% at 3.6 mg/kg. That figure is an unpublished phase 1 readout and may shrink, but a near coin-flip response against a target he is proven to express, in his line, is the best expected-value bet on this list. Six Northeast sites including MSK and MGH make screening practical now, in parallel with the HER2 workup.
primary_concerns: The 47% ORR is an ASCO 2026 initial result from a dose-escalation study, not a published estimate; regression toward something smaller is likely.
Contemporary Nectin-4 expression after ~25 months of EV is unverified, and primary-to-node IHC agreement in urothelial cancer is only moderate (kappa 0.41).
Cohort B2 requires measurable disease, which the SBRT-treated nodal sites may fail.
A topoisomerase I payload brings its own GI toxicity onto an active severe-nausea problem.

picks.intervention_label: [225Ac]Ac-AKY-1189 (Nectin-4 actinium-225 radioligand), NCT07020117
picks.rationale: An alpha emitter kills by crossfire, so it needs neither uniform antigen nor internalization, which is the insurance you want if EV thinned Nectin-4 expression. The 64Cu imaging step answers the current-expression question during screening and spends no tissue, in a case down to one frozen vial. Prior EV is explicitly permitted, which almost no other Nectin-4 protocol allows, and Mount Sinai is enrolling. There is no human efficacy data at all, so this is a pure mechanism bet, but it is the one Nectin-4 route insulated from both the MMAE problem and antigen heterogeneity at once.
primary_concerns: First-in-human dose escalation with zero efficacy data; he could be treated at a subtherapeutic dose level.
Measurable RECIST disease after SBRT to the only known nodal sites is a real screening gate.
Renal handling of an actinium-225 ligand matters and his creatinine/eGFR is not even in the available record, with a history of obstructive uropathy.
The 3-week washout from T-DXd forces a sequencing decision before the HER2 question is settled.

picks.intervention_label: ipilimumab addition to PD-1 blockade (nivolumab 1 mg/kg + ipilimumab 3 mg/kg / TITAN-TCC boost strategy)
picks.rationale: TITAN-TCC produced a 33% ITT response rate using high-dose ipilimumab boosts in urothelial patients who had already failed PD-1, and CheckMate 032 showed response climbing with ipilimumab dose to 38% at nivo1/ipi3. A deep 25-month response to an IO-containing regimen, TMB 12.4 mut/Mb, and progression only on maintenance is the profile where adding CTLA-4 has actually rescued patients. Both drugs are prescribable off-label today, with no screening assay, no manufacturing slot, and no washout beyond clinical judgment. The 2025 checkpoint pancreatitis is the honest hazard, and TITAN-TCC had two enterocolitis deaths in 83 patients, so this needs eyes-open consent rather than avoidance.
primary_concerns: Prior immune-related pancreatitis (lipase 3x ULN, 2025) makes recurrence on CTLA-4 escalation a genuine risk; the q3-4wk amylase/lipase surveillance already in place helps but does not remove it.
He progressed on pembrolizumab maintenance, so the marginal benefit of re-intensifying the same axis is unproven in him.
TITAN-TCC and CheckMate 032 both required prior platinum, which he never had; the transfer is imperfect.
TMB 12.4 was measured on an institutional panel, not the assay the TMB-H threshold was validated on.

picks.intervention_label: CLSP-1025 (TP53 R175H x HLA-A*02:01 T-cell engager), NCT06778863
picks.rationale: Both eligibility gates are already answered in his record: HLA-A*02:01 on 2025-01 typing and TP53 R175H in plasma. An off-the-shelf engager needs no manufacturing runway, four sites sit inside his care orbit, and the preclinical package behind the format, structure-resolved specificity in Science 2021 plus the affinity work showing the engager beats CAR formats at this antigen density, is unusually deep for a first-in-human program. The only human precedent on this axis is a single TCR-T patient with a 55% regression lasting 6 months, so the shot is thin, but it aims at a truncal driver mutation the tumor cannot shed the way it can shed a surface antigen. Request tissue confirmation of R175H in parallel with screening, not as a precondition for it.
primary_concerns: The R175H call rests on one plasma read at 0.09% VAF; the sponsor's central test could simply fail to confirm it, or the variant could be subclonal.
No clinical data exist for CLSP-1025 or any agent in its class; CRS and off-tumor behavior in humans are unknown.
Dose escalation means possible enrollment at a dose nobody expects to work.
Peptide-HLA copy number per cell is very low, which the preclinical lineage itself flags as the shared obstacle.

notes: Two high-response options were left off deliberately rather than overlooked. Disitamab vedotin has the best HER2 response rate in urothelial cancer (ORR 50.5%, pmid:37988648) but its MMAE payload put 68.2% of patients into sensory neuropathy, straight into the CIPN veto, and every US cohort excludes him anyway (prior HER2 therapy, prior MMAE ADC). Trastuzumab plus paclitaxel (pmid:37385153) fails the same veto through its taxane. AVZO-103 (NCT07193511) nearly made the list, covering Nectin-4 and TROP2 in one agent, but its drug-induced-ILD exclusion collides with the unresolved 2026-03 chest CT and I ranked the two Nectin-4 routes without that gate instead. The mesothelin axis stays off the ranking on results, not principle: the strong stain is research-grade, huCART-meso posted 0% ORR (pmid:41566776) and the one randomized mesothelin-selected ADC trial was negative (pmid:35358455). Biggest threat to this whole ranking: the unretrieved NGS report. One OncoKB-actionable alteration is sitting unnamed in a 2023 report, and FGFR3 status would open erdafitinib and FORAGER-1 cohort B7; that records request could reorder everything above.

picks.intervention_label: trastuzumab deruxtecan (T-DXd), continued only if three named conditions hold
picks.rationale: This is the one option on-label for this exact patient (tumor-agnostic HER2 IHC 3+ approval, NCCN-listed) and the one with a mature safety file: pooled monotherapy analyses cover 1,150 to 2,145 patients, ILD is managed under an established adjudication-and-steroid algorithm, and the nausea now limiting dosing is a known quantity (74.6% any grade at 5.4 mg/kg, mostly grade 1-2) for which dose reduction is the modal fix (22.6%). Bladder-cohort ORR at central IHC 3+ was 56.3% (95% CI 29.9-80.2, n=16). Continuation is strictly conditional: the 2026-08 repeat validated IHC must stay 3+, the conflicting 2026-03 chest CT read must be resolved before the next dose because pre-existing lung comorbidity is a named baseline ILD risk factor and adjudicated drug-related ILD ran 10.5% with three fatal cases in DESTINY-PanTumor02, and antiemetic prophylaxis needs formal escalation with a dose-reduction plan. If any of the three fails, stopping beats improvising.
primary_concerns: Two of the four inferred toxicity vetoes are already engaged: severe nausea after dose 2 (GI veto) and the unresolved 2026-03 ILD-suggestive CT read (ILD veto); the pooled analysis (pmid:35963179) also found adjudicated ILD onset preceded investigator recognition by a median of 43 days, so baseline imaging ambiguity has a direct cost
HER2 status of the CURRENT tumor is unsettled; a downgrade to 2+ or 1+ moves this from on-label use to cross-tumor extrapolation from breast trials, a much weaker footing
The bladder IHC 3+ efficacy estimate rests on 16 patients with a 29.9-80.2 confidence interval

picks.intervention_label: pertuzumab plus trastuzumab (TAPUR arm or off-label, pending ERBB2 report)
picks.rationale: Both antibodies carry well over a decade of post-marketing safety data (trastuzumab since 1998, pertuzumab since 2012), biosimilar supply, and a payload-free toxicity profile: in MyPathway the leading events were diarrhoea 36.1%, fatigue 29.4% and nausea 22.4%, no single serious term exceeded 1.7%, and cardiac monitoring follows a standard LVEF algorithm. This is the only HER2 option in the dossier that touches none of the four stated vetoes. The tradeoff is efficacy: ORR 41.0% at IHC 3+ amplified but 25.9% overall, activity after T-DXd exposure is untested, and the TAPUR arm turns on ERBB2 amplification or overexpression documented in the still-unretrieved full NGS report. I am ranking the safer HER2 route above the more active ones and saying so plainly.
primary_concerns: Off-label and off-guideline in urothelial carcinoma; the protocolized route (TAPUR) is gated on a qualifying ERBB2 genomic report nobody has retrieved yet
MyPathway's IHC-tier gradient (41% at 3+, 8.3% at 1+, 0% at IHC 0) means the pending re-stain decides whether this option has a floor at all
No data on activity in T-DXd-exposed tumors; the basket predates that sequencing question

picks.intervention_label: nivolumab plus ipilimumab (checkpoint re-intensification, lower-ipilimumab schedule)
picks.rationale: Both drugs are FDA-approved with roughly a decade of post-marketing irAE experience and management algorithms codified in ASCO and NCCN guidance, which is the safety infrastructure I want behind any next systemic move. TITAN-TCC tested the exact manoeuvre the care team is weighing, an ipilimumab boost after PD-1 failure: ITT ORR 33% (90% CI 24-42) against a prespecified 20% bar, but immune-mediated enterocolitis reached 11% grade 3-4 and accounted for both treatment-related deaths (2/83). CheckMate 032 shows the toxicity is dose-dependent, grade 3-4 TRAEs rising from 26.9% with nivolumab alone to 39.1% at nivo1/ipi3, so the gentler schedule is the defensible one here. The 2025 checkpoint-associated pancreatitis (lipase peak 384 U/L) sits on the stated pancreatitis veto; continued q3-4wk amylase/lipase surveillance would need to be a formal condition, not a habit.
primary_concerns: Prior immune-related pancreatitis makes CTLA-4 addition a rechallenge with a steeper irAE curve; the pancreatitis-risk veto applies unless surveillance and stopping rules are protocolized up front
The doublet is off-label and off-guideline in urothelial carcinoma, so payer friction is part of the safety-of-execution picture
Neither trial population matches this course: TITAN-TCC required prior platinum and CheckMate 032 was checkpoint-naive, and this patient progressed on pembrolizumab maintenance

picks.intervention_label: zanidatamab (payload-free HER2 bispecific), fallback if 3+ holds but T-DXd stops
picks.rationale: Included reluctantly, as the payload-free fallback if the re-stain stays 3+ but T-DXd is stopped for tolerability: with no cytotoxic payload the neuropathy, ILD, emesis and pancreatitis vetoes do not bite, and the phase 1 safety file was benign, six grade 3 treatment-related events in 4 of 132 patients and no treatment-related deaths. Everything else fails my usual tests: first-in-human single-arm evidence, ORR 37.0% (95% CI 27.0-48.7) driven largely by biliary tract disease, and an accelerated approval dating only to 2024-11. The missing safety datum is time on market, under two years against the five I usually ask for. The pan-tumor trial cohort bars prior HER2-directed therapy, so the realistic route is off-label prescription, which stands or falls with the IHC tier.
primary_concerns: Phase-1 single-arm evidence outside biliary tract cancer; response durability in urothelial carcinoma is unknown
Post-approval safety follow-up is under two years, far short of the long-tail window in which antibody-class toxicities declare themselves
Prior T-DXd closes the registered trial cohort, and the off-label payer case collapses if the repeat IHC comes back below 3+

notes: Interventions I declined to rank, with the specific safety datum that disqualifies each rather than a novelty reflex: disitamab vedotin (ORR 50.5% is the best HER2 number in urothelial carcinoma, but 68.2% any-grade and 18.7% grade >=3 sensory neuropathy on an MMAE payload against established CIPN violates the neuropathy veto, and no non-MMAE formulation data exist; pmid:37988648); trastuzumab plus paclitaxel (88.9% any-grade neuropathy from the taxane backbone; pmid:37385153); enfortumab vedotin rechallenge (same MMAE-CIPN collision, and the only published rechallenge cohort covers skin toxicity in 20 patients, not neuropathy; pmid:41578675); sacituzumab govitecan (negative confirmatory phase 3, OS HR 0.86 p=0.087, grade 5 TEAEs 7% mostly neutropenic infections, urothelial approval withdrawn 2024; pmid:39934055); pembrolizumab re-challenge alone (progression occurred on maintenance, and the TMB-H cutoff was validated on FoundationOne CDx, not the institutional panel that produced 12.4 mut/Mb; pmid:32919526); every CAR-T, T-cell engager, TCR, radioligand and ATR-inhibitor row (phase 1 or case-series evidence with no post-marketing safety follow-up at all, several with named fatal-toxicity signals). The preferences file weights efficacy at 0.7 and leans experimental; my job on this board is to be the counterweight, and the counterweight still found four options with real safety files. The single most valuable near-term action is not a drug at all: retrieve the 2026-08 HER2 and TROP2 IHC tiers and the full NGS report (ERBB2 amplification, FGFR3, the unnamed OncoKB-actionable alteration) before committing to any branch.

picks.intervention_label: trastuzumab deruxtecan (T-DXd), continue only if the 2026-08 validated HER2 IHC reads 3+ and the chest CT discrepancy is adjudicated
picks.rationale: The tumor-agnostic label rests on DESTINY-PanTumor02, an open-label single-arm phase 2 with no comparator and ORR as the endpoint, and the bladder IHC 3+ estimate is 16 patients (ORR 56.3%, 95% CI 29.9-80.2). What keeps it at rank 1 anyway is replication: MyPathway shows the same expression gradient (41% ORR at IHC 3+, 8.3% at 1+, zero at IHC 0), and two randomized phase 3 breast trials hit registered PFS endpoints at p<0.001, so the drug and the biomarker logic are not a one-study artifact. Continuation is defensible only if the pending 2026-08 validated stain reads 3+; a downgrade moves this to cross-tumor extrapolation from breast, which is a different and weaker claim than on-label use. Adjudicated drug-related ILD ran 10.5% with three deaths in the pivotal cohort, and pre-existing lung disease is a named risk factor, so the unresolved 2026-03 chest CT read is a precondition, not a footnote.
primary_concerns: ROBINS-I moderate on the pivotal trial: single-arm, open-label, no comparator, ORR surrogate; the confirmatory randomized evidence sits in breast cancer, not urothelial
Tier-matched bladder subgroup is n=16 with a 95% CI of 29.9-80.2; the number the decision leans on is the least precise one in the row
Selection and measurement bias in the current decision: the three IHC 3+ results describe 2023-2025 tumor, and the 2026-08 validated tier on contemporary tissue is drawn but unretrieved

ILD/pneumonitis 10.5% (1.5% grade >=3, three fatal) in the pivotal cohort and 15.4% pooled, with pre-existing lung comorbidity a baseline risk factor; the 2026-03 versus 2026-06 chest CT conflict is unresolved
Tolerability already grade-limiting: severe nausea after dose 2, against a pooled any-grade nausea rate of 74.6% at 5.4 mg/kg

picks.intervention_label: ipilimumab added to PD-1 blockade (TITAN-TCC boost schema)
picks.rationale: TITAN-TCC is the rare single-arm trial built the way I want one built: a registered primary endpoint with a prespecified 20% response threshold, met at 33% (90% CI 24-42, p=0.0049), testing the exact maneuver in question, an ipilimumab boost after PD-1 failure in urothelial carcinoma. CheckMate 032 independently shows response climbing with ipilimumab dose (38% at nivo1/ipi3 versus 25.6% for nivolumab alone), so the CTLA-4 contribution is replicated across two trials rather than read off one. Neither population matches this course: both required prior platinum, CheckMate 032 was checkpoint-naive, and progression here was on pembrolizumab maintenance, not nivolumab. Two enterocolitis deaths in 83 TITAN-TCC patients have to be weighed against the 2025 checkpoint-associated pancreatitis.
primary_concerns: No randomized comparison anywhere in the class for this setting; TITAN-TCC's comparator is a historical nivolumab ORR from CheckMate 275, which is the ROBINS-I confounding domain by construction
Population transfer: both supporting trials enrolled post-platinum patients and this patient never received platinum; the boost data are after nivolumab failure, not pembrolizumab maintenance failure
ORR surrogate with no OS or PFS claim for the boost strategy
Grade 3-4 treatment-related AEs 39.1% at nivo1/ipi3 and treatment-related deaths 2/83 from enterocolitis, in a patient with prior immune-mediated pancreatitis and lipase surveillance still running

picks.intervention_label: LY4052031 (Nectin-4 ADC, camptothecin payload) via NEXUS-01 cohort B2
picks.rationale: The target is the best-validated thing in this dossier: Nectin-4 ADC therapy has two randomized phase 3 OS wins in urothelial carcinoma (EV-301 HR 0.70, p=0.001; EV-302 HR 0.47, p<0.001), and this patient's own 25-month complete response is consistent with both. The agent is another matter: the 47% post-EV response figure comes from an ASCO 2026 abstract of an ongoing sponsor-run phase 1, unpublished and not peer reviewed, so I treat it as a screening lead and not as evidence. Contemporary Nectin-4 expression after 25 months of enfortumab vedotin is unverified, antigen downregulation is a recognized resistance route, and the 2026-06 imaging read should be retrieved before a slot is spent. Rank 3 reflects RCT-grade target validation plus a payload that avoids the MMAE neuropathy veto, not confidence in this drug.
primary_concerns: Agent-level evidence is a conference abstract from an open-label dose-escalation study; no published response, durability or safety data exist to appraise for bias
The phase 3 support attaches to a different drug and payload in a post-platinum population; carryover to a topoisomerase-payload agent after prolonged EV is assumed, not demonstrated
Both Nectin-4 stains predate EV exposure; a re-targeting decision on 2023-2025 expression repeats the same error the HER2 branch is trying to avoid
Screening gates unresolved: measurable disease after SBRT to the only known node, and the T-DXd washout with sequential topoisomerase-I exposure unstudied

picks.intervention_label: trastuzumab plus pertuzumab via the TAPUR HER2 arm, conditional on ERBB2 amplification in the retrieved NGS report
picks.rationale: MyPathway is a non-randomized basket and I grade it ROBINS-I serious, but it is also the study that quantifies the HER2 tier gradient this whole case turns on: 41% ORR at amplified IHC 3+, falling to 8.3% at 1+ and zero at IHC 0, with two of the five complete responses in urothelial tumors. No cytotoxic payload means neither the neuropathy veto nor the deruxtecan ILD class problem applies, which matters when nearly every other HER2 row collides with one or both. The arm is conditional twice over: ERBB2 amplification sits unread in the 2023 NGS report, and activity of naked HER2 antibodies after progression on a HER2 ADC is undocumented in this tumor type. It earns rank 4 because the drugs are approved, access is protocolized, and the evidence base, while single-arm, is internally consistent and fully disclosed.
primary_concerns: ROBINS-I serious: open-label basket, no comparator, ORR surrogate, and KRAS status confounds the pooled estimate (28.1% wild-type versus 7.1% mutant)
The urothelial signal is two complete responses inside a 263-patient pooled cohort; no urothelial-specific confidence interval exists
Conditional on an unretrieved NGS report; the same retrieval could surface an FGFR3 alteration and an approved oral option that outranks this row
No data on naked-antibody activity after T-DXd exposure; ADC-resistant tumors may have already selected against the target

notes: What I declined carries as much information as the ranking. Sacituzumab govitecan failed its confirmatory phase 3 (TROPiCS-04, OS HR 0.86, p=0.087) and the urothelial approval was withdrawn; a higher response rate that does not move survival is the exact surrogate trap this board exists to catch. The mesothelin axis has a prospectively expression-selected negative RCT (ARCS-M, PFS HR 1.22) and a 0/20 ORR CAR-T series, so a strong research-grade stain changes nothing until a validated assay and a better construct both exist. MUC1 has no response evidence in any tumor type relevant here. IMA203 reports 28.9% confirmed ORR with a 4.4-month median duration, all in melanoma and sarcoma, on the sponsor's own expression assay, with the PRAME gate for this patient still unread. The vaccine axis is already running and its randomized support (KEYNOTE-942, RFS HR 0.51) is adjuvant melanoma, not metastatic urothelial cancer; this patient's own EliSpot, 2 of 14 evaluable pools and CD4-skewed, sits at the weak end of the Rojas response distribution, and ctDNA rose through most of the vaccine period. The TP53 R175H engager and TCR-T trials have no published clinical results and the variant call rests on a single 0.09% VAF plasma read. Ceralasertib's 14% ORR came entirely from gynecologic histologies. Last point, and the one I would put first in clinic: the cheapest evidence upgrades in this case are not drugs. The 2026-08 HER2 and TROP2 tiers, the ERBB2 copy number, the FGFR3 status and the unnamed OncoKB-actionable alteration all sit in reports already generated and never retrieved. None of my four picks survives unchanged if those reads come back adverse.

picks.intervention_label: trastuzumab deruxtecan (T-DXd), continue pending HER2 reconciliation
picks.rationale: The one feature-matched option here with real cross-body consensus: FDA tumor-agnostic accelerated approval (2024-04-05) for HER2 IHC 3+ solid tumors after prior systemic therapy, and NCCN Bladder Cancer v1.2026 carries it as the biomarker-directed subsequent-line option after enfortumab vedotin plus pembrolizumab (category 2A). Three validated IHC 3+ results put this patient inside the labeled population, and the bladder IHC 3+ cohort of DESTINY-PanTumor02 responded at 56.3%. Continuation should hang on the pending validated re-stain, because the label and the guideline both require 3+, not the research MXIF signal.
primary_concerns: The guideline population is defined by validated IHC 3+ on tumor tissue; the pending 2026-08 re-stain can move him out of it, and a 2+ or lower result turns continuation into off-label extrapolation from DESTINY-Breast04 (pmid:35665782), which no urothelial guideline covers.

Adjudicated drug-related ILD was 10.5% in DESTINY-PanTumor02 and pre-existing lung comorbidity is a named risk factor in the pooled safety analysis (pmid:35963179); the unresolved 2026-03 outside CT read has to be reconciled before the next dose.

Severe nausea after dose 2 runs into the stated GI veto; the guideline-consistent response is antiemetic escalation and dose modification (the modal response in the pooled trials, pmid:41330717) before abandoning the class.
The bladder IHC 3+ estimate rests on 16 patients, so the tier-matched effect size is wide.

picks.intervention_label: FGFR3 axis, conditional: retrieve NGS report; erdafitinib if altered, vepugratinib trial (NCT05614739) as the investigational arm
picks.rationale: The only other biomarker route both major bodies endorse in urothelial carcinoma is FGFR: the ESMO Clinical Practice Guideline interim update on first-line therapy in advanced urothelial carcinoma (Ann Oncol 2024) names erdafitinib for FGFR-altered tumours after enfortumab vedotin plus pembrolizumab, and NCCN Bladder Cancer v1.2026 lists erdafitinib for susceptible FGFR3 alterations (category 2A). This patient's FGFR3 status is simply missing from the record, and the full NGS report already exists. Retrieve it; if an FGFR3 alteration turns up, the guideline-endorsed drug or the vepugratinib trial (NCT05614739) becomes the strongest non-HER2 branch on this board.
primary_concerns: Wholly conditional on a records-retrieval step, and most metastatic urothelial patients (roughly 80-85%) carry no qualifying FGFR3 alteration, so the expected yield is modest.
The consensus standing belongs to erdafitinib; vepugratinib itself is phase 1 and off-guideline, so if the alteration is found the approved drug is the default and the trial is the escalation.

picks.intervention_label: sacituzumab tirumotecan (sac-TMT) phase 3 trial, NCT07419295, TROP2 axis via randomized enrollment
picks.rationale: No guideline endorses a TROP2 agent in urothelial carcinoma today, and the class precedent is a withdrawal: Gilead pulled the sacituzumab govitecan accelerated approval on 2024-10-18 after TROPiCS-04 missed overall survival (pmid:39934055). Where consensus is absent, the guideline-aligned move is a randomized trial, and NCT07419295 is a phase 3 of sacituzumab tirumotecan against chemotherapy in exactly this post-EV, post-checkpoint space. Enrolling is the way to reach a TROP2 agent without stepping outside the evidence framework NCCN and ESMO actually operate on.
primary_concerns: The comparator arm is a taxane or vinflunine, and a taxane assignment would run straight into his established CIPN; that risk is inherent to randomization.
His TROP2 read is low-positive on a research assay; SG benefit was seen across expression levels (pmid:39086310), but weak expression stays a weaker predictor.
Back-to-back topoisomerase I payloads after T-DXd and the washout window need sponsor input before screening.

picks.intervention_label: zanidatamab (HER2 biparatopic bispecific), phase 2 trial NCT06695845, payload-free HER2 fallback
picks.rationale: If the re-stain confirms 3+ but GI intolerance forces a switch, the HER2 axis should not be abandoned, and zanidatamab is the payload-free way to stay on it: 37% ORR across HER2-expressing tumors in the phase 1 (NCT02892123) with almost no grade 3 toxicity, now enrolling in phase 2 (NCT06695845). No guideline lists it in urothelial carcinoma, so this is a trial-only fallback and it is ranked like one.
primary_concerns: Registered pan-tumor cohorts have barred prior HER2-directed therapy, which the current T-DXd course triggers; screening has to settle that before this option is real.
Durability outside biliary tract cancer is thin, and the 37% ORR is a phase 1 estimate across mixed histologies.

notes: Guideline positions verified by web on 2026-08-20: FDA tumor-agnostic T-DXd approval for IHC 3+ (fda.gov, 2024-04-05); NCCN Bladder Cancer v1.2026 T-DXd listing as the biomarker-directed option after EV plus pembrolizumab (tier language sourced from the JNCCN 2025 supplement summary and the 2026 NCCN patient guideline; the guideline PDF itself is login-gated, so the category 2A reading rests on NCCN's default-category convention and should be spot-checked in round 2); ESMO Clinical Practice Guideline interim update on first-line therapy in advanced urothelial carcinoma (Ann Oncol 2024) for post-EV+P sequencing; Gilead withdrawal of the sacituzumab govitecan mUC indication (2024-10-18). Three deliberate omissions. First, the guideline-preferred next systemic line for a platinum-naive patient after EV plus pembrolizumab is platinum-based chemotherapy per that same ESMO interim update; that belongs to the standard-of-care track, not this ranking, and it subtracts nothing from the picks above. Second, disitamab vedotin has the best HER2 response numbers in urothelial carcinoma (pmid:37988648) but its guideline standing is CSCO (China) only, its US trials exclude prior HER2-directed therapy, and the MMAE payload runs into the neuropathy veto, so it stays off my list on the persona's own rules. Third, pembrolizumab's TMB-H tumor-agnostic standing does not survive progression on pembrolizumab maintenance, and nivolumab plus ipilimumab has no NCCN listing in urothelial carcinoma, so the checkpoint re-intensification axis has no consensus footing I can rank.

picks.intervention_label: LY4052031 (Nectin-4 ADC, camptothecin payload), NEXUS-01 cohort B2
picks.rationale: Cohort B2 is written for this exact history: urothelial carcinoma with prior enfortumab vedotin required rather than excluded, and a camptothecin payload in place of the MMAE that drove 25 months of dose reductions and the neuropathy this file vetoes. Reported response in post-EV participants was 47% at 3.6 mg/kg, the strongest efficacy number on offer to a patient weighted 0.7 toward efficacy. Screening runs on histology and prior therapy rather than a fresh biopsy, so it spends none of the one remaining fresh-frozen vial. Two gates are real and neither is trivial: a measurable lesion outside the SBRT field, and two topoisomerase-I payloads back to back after T-DXd, which nobody has studied.
primary_concerns: Cross-resistance between the deruxtecan payload the patient is on now and the camptothecin payload here is unstudied; the investigator should be asked directly rather than after enrollment.
Measurable disease is the recurring problem across every ADC row: the only known lesion was irradiated in 2026-06 and a baseline re-read has to establish a target.
Camptothecin-class payloads bring diarrhea and neutropenia, which sits next to the active GI intolerance rather than clear of it.
Enrollment cannot be discussed until the T-DXd stop decision is made, so this option is hostage to the HER2 tier and the ctDNA kinetics.

picks.intervention_label: [225Ac]Ac-AKY-1189 (Nectin-4 actinium-225 radioligand) with [64Cu]Cu-AKY-1189 imaging
picks.rationale: The 64Cu imaging step is what makes this fit the patient's constraints: it answers whether the node still carries Nectin-4 with a scan instead of a slide, which is precisely what the tissue-scarcity note asks for. Prior EV is permitted outright, and an alpha emitter kills by crossfire rather than needing antigen on every cell, so partial antigen loss after 25 months of EV does not sink it. There is no MMAE payload and no deruxtecan payload, so neither the neuropathy veto nor the ILD veto bites. Honest accounting: this is first-in-human dose escalation with no efficacy data, so the argument is mechanism and preference fit, not a number.
primary_concerns: Zero clinical efficacy data. Ranking it second is a bet on fit, and the patient should hear it framed that way.
Marrow toxicity from an alpha radioligand deserves attention in a man with a 2025 iron-deficiency anemia history and platelets at 170.
Same measurable-lesion gate as the other post-EV trials, plus a roughly 3-week washout from T-DXd.
The 2026-06 Nectin-4 imaging read is still not in the record; retrieving it could make this screening visit unnecessary or much more attractive.

picks.intervention_label: CLSP-1025 (TP53 R175H x HLA-A*02:01 T-cell engager), GUARDIAN-101
picks.rationale: Both eligibility gates are already answered in this record without cutting tissue: HLA-A*02:01 on the 2025-01 typing and TP53 R175H on the 2025-06 plasma draw. An off-the-shelf engager needs no apheresis slot and no manufacturing wait, histology is open, and four sites sit inside the patient's usual care orbit. The 0.09% VAF plasma read is thin evidence that the current clone carries R175H, and the sponsor's central confirmation is where this holds or fails, so checking whether the 2023 tissue panel specified R175H comes first. No clinical readout exists for this class yet, only its preclinical lineage, which is the risk an efficacy-leaning posture is buying here.
primary_concerns: A single 0.09% VAF plasma call is a weak basis for a whole eligibility case; tissue-level confirmation of R175H should be pulled from the existing NGS report before a screening visit.
Peptide-HLA copy number on the tumor surface is low for every agent in this class, which is the shared obstacle the preclinical work keeps running into.
Cytokine release syndrome is the expected toxicity; it does not trip any stated veto, but it does mean inpatient step-up dosing.
Tumor HLA-A*02 loss of heterozygosity is unmeasured and computable from existing exome data; if the allele is lost, this pick and the PRAME axis both weaken at once.

picks.intervention_label: FT825 / ONO-8250 (off-the-shelf iPSC-derived HER2 CAR-T)
picks.rationale: If the HER2 branch continues at all, this is the version that survives the file's constraints: an allogeneic product needs no apheresis, prior HER2-directed therapy is not an exclusion, and there is no deruxtecan payload to argue with the 2026-03 chest CT read. Yale, MSK and Jefferson are enrolling. It still waits on the 2026-08 validated HER2 tier, because HER2 benefit tracks the stain rather than running independent of it: 61.3% response at central IHC 3+ in DESTINY-PanTumor02, and 41% falling to 8.3% at IHC 1+ in MyPathway. Conditioning chemotherapy and CRS are real, and the ongoing mRNA vaccine series has to be cleared against the prior-gene-therapy exclusion before anyone books a screening slot.
primary_concerns: Gated entirely on the pending validated HER2 tier; if the current tumor is HER2-low, the whole branch drops to cross-tumor extrapolation.
The prior cell or gene therapy exclusion is a live question given two vaccine programs, and it should be asked before rather than during screening.
Lymphodepleting conditioning in a patient with chronic CIPN and a pancreatitis history needs the toxicity conversation up front.
Phase 1 dose escalation in HER2-expressing solid tumors, with no urothelial efficacy signal to quote.

picks.intervention_label: ASP2998 (TROP2-directed STING agonist conjugate), monotherapy or pembrolizumab arm
picks.rationale: Urothelial carcinoma is a named escalation and expansion histology with no cap on prior regimens, and prior TROP2 or topoisomerase-I exposure is permitted, so the T-DXd course does not close this door the way it closes the zanidatamab and NEOK002 rows. A STING-agonist payload is a different bet from a cytotoxic ADC and should depend less on antigen density, which suits a weak TROP2 stain; the TROPHY-U-01 biomarker analysis found benefit across expression levels, though almost everyone studied sat well above this patient's low signal. The enfortumab vedotin combination arms should be declined at first contact, and that preference stated in writing, because an MMAE arm would walk straight into the neuropathy veto. Phase 1 with no efficacy data, and an immune-agonist payload in a man with checkpoint-associated pancreatitis in 2025 means lipase surveillance belongs in the plan rather than in the follow-up.
primary_concerns: Randomization or assignment to an enfortumab vedotin combination arm would violate the neuropathy veto; the arm preference has to be settled with the site before consent.
This patient's TROP2 signal sits below almost the entire TROPHY-U-01 distribution, so expression-agnostic entry is not the same as expression-agnostic benefit.
STING agonism is an inflammatory mechanism in a patient whose 2025 pancreatitis arose on immunotherapy; q3-4wk lipase monitoring should continue on study.
The validated 2026-08 TROP2 tier is still unretrieved, and it calibrates how much weight this axis deserves.

notes: Three things the preference file forces me to say out loud. First, the current therapy: T-DXd already collides with two stated vetoes at once, severe GI toxicity (severe nausea and bloating after dose 2, against a pooled nausea rate of 74.6% at 5.4 mg/kg) and ILD risk against an unresolved 2026-03 chest CT read suggestive of fibrosis, with adjudicated drug-related ILD at 10.5% and three deaths in DESTINY-PanTumor02. Continuing it without an antiemetic plan and a pulmonology adjudication is not a preference-respecting choice, and the label it rests on is written for IHC 3+ on a stain nobody has read yet. Second, the ipilimumab addition the care team is exploring is the option I most want to like and cannot rank: TITAN-TCC reached 33% response after PD-1 failure, but 11% grade 3-4 immune enterocolitis with two treatment-related deaths sits on the severe GI veto and the 2025 checkpoint-associated pancreatitis sits on the pancreatitis veto. That is two vetoes on one regimen, and it belongs in the conversation with the patient rather than in my ranked list. Third, AVZO-103 covers both the Nectin-4 and TROP2 features in one agent with sites in New Haven and New York, and I would have ranked it second or third if the ILD question were settled; its own exclusion for drug-induced ILD is what keeps it off. Every pick above is a trial, which is what prefers_trials asked for, and four of the five screen on blood, imaging or existing reports rather than a fresh biopsy. The data-retrieval items in the free-text constraints, the 2026-08 HER2 and TROP2 tiers, the 2026-06 Nectin-4 imaging read and the full NGS report with FGFR3 status, are worth more to this patient right now than any single row I have ranked; if FGFR3 comes back altered, FORAGER-1 cohort B7 or erdafitinib would displace most of this list.
